title: Investigatio motuum, quibus laminae et virgae elasticae contremiscunt

deep.reconstruction: This page completes Case III of §30: a uniform elastic rod (Euler-Bernoulli beam) that is free at the end E (s=0) and clamped at F (s=a). It is the cantilever problem. Euler takes the mode y = α e^{s/f} + β e^{-s/f} + γ sin(s/f) + δ cos(s/f), with time factor sin(ζ + t√(2g/k)). The free-end conditions y''(0)=0 and y'''(0)=0 give δ = α+β and γ = α−β. Clamping at s=a, with ω = a/f, means y(a)=0 and y'(a)=0. These give two linear homogeneous equations in α and β. Write p = sin ω + cos ω and q = sin ω − cos ω. Setting the two expressions for α/β equal and cross-multiplying gives 2 + (p−q)(e^ω+e^{−ω}) + p²+q² = 0. Since p²+q² = 2 and p−q = 2cos ω, this reduces to cos ω = −2/(e^ω+e^{−ω}). In modern form that is the cantilever frequency equation cos ω cosh ω = −1. Euler concludes that cos ω < 0, so the roots lie in quadrants 2,3; 6,7; 10,11; and so on. This is correct: the roots ≈1.875, 4.694, 7.855, 10.996 lie in exactly those quadrants, one per quadrant. He then gets sin ω = ±tanh ω and treats the two sign cases separately. For sin ω = tanh ω he simplifies to α/β = e^{−ω}; for the other sign, α/β = −e^{−ω}. Normalising α = 1 gives β = ±e^ω, γ = 1 ∓ e^ω, δ = 1 ± e^ω. The mode shape is therefore y = C sin(ζ + t√(2g/k)) [e^{uω} ± e^{ω(1−u)} + (1∓e^ω) sin uω + (1±e^ω) cos uω], with u = s/a. Here f = a/ω, k = a⁴/(b c² ω⁴) and √(2g/k) = ω² c√(2gb)/a². On the next page the frequency follows as ∝ ω²/a², and the roots ω are found numerically in the corollaries.
errors: None of substance. Every algebraic step checks: the cross-multiplication, the reduction to cos ω cosh ω = −1, sin ω = ±tanh ω, and the simplification of α/β to ±e^{−ω}. The sign case alternates from root to root (sin ω>0 for ω≈1.875, <0 for ω≈4.694, and so on), which matches Euler's warning that the two cases must be carefully distinguished.

ideas.what: Frequency equation of the clamped-free (cantilever) beam, cos ω cosh ω = −1
ideas.modern_name: Cantilever beam characteristic equation (Euler-Bernoulli beam theory)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Daniel Bernoulli and Euler (1742-1744); Euler's E65 Additamentum on elastic curves
ideas.where_published: E65 (Methodus inveniendi, 1744, Additamentum I) treats the clamped-free lamina; E526 reworks the cases systematically; discussed in Truesdell's Rational Mechanics of Flexible or Elastic Bodies (Opera omnia II.11)

ideas.what: Root location: cos ω<0 places the eigenvalues in quadrants 2,3,6,7,10,11,...
ideas.modern_name: Root localisation / interlacing of beam eigenvalues near (2n−1)π/2

ideas.what: Closed-form cantilever mode shapes, with the sign case sin ω = ±tanh ω giving α/β = ±e^{−ω}
ideas.modern_name: Cantilever beam mode shapes (Rayleigh / Strutt form, cosh−cos−σ(sinh−sin))
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler, D. Bernoulli; later standardised by Rayleigh and Strutt

deep.surprise_reason: This is a standard, correct derivation of the well-known cantilever frequency equation and mode shapes. Euler's priority here, with D. Bernoulli, is already documented by Truesdell. Nothing on the page appears new to the literature.
transcription_corrections: In the time factor the variable is t: 'ζ + t√(2g/k)', as in the image.
On the previous page, 'fin. ω − cof. ω = g' should read '= q', and 'terminos liber' should read 'terminus liber'.
